pages.html:
Hydro dipping, also known as water transfer printing, is a process that allows for the application of intricate designs to three-dimensional objects. It involves submerging an item in water that has a special film floating on its surface, which contains the desired pattern or graphic. When the object is dipped into the water, the film adheres to its surface, wrapping around curves and contours for a seamless finish. This technique is popular for customizing items like automotive parts, helmets, and various consumer goods, offering a wide range of designs, from camo patterns to vibrant graphics. Hydro dipping not only enhances aesthetics but also provides a protective layer to the underlying material.

We can print any image onto onto a specialist hydrographic film. This allows us to make your products completely bespoke to you. We specialise in the hydro dipping of car parts which can be anything from mirrors, alloy wheels, trims or even the dashboard.

Hydro dipping, also known as water transfer printing, is a popular method for customizing car parts with unique designs. Here’s a brief overview of the process:

1. Preparation

  • Clean the Parts: Thoroughly clean the car parts to remove dirt, grease, and any old paint. This helps the hydro dip adhere better.
  • Sanding: Lightly sand the surface to create a better grip for the paint.
  • Priming: Apply a primer suitable for the material of the part to enhance adhesion and finish.

2. Choosing the Film

  • Select a hydrographic film with the desired pattern or design (camouflage, carbon fiber, etc.). Ensure it’s compatible with the type of paint you’re using.

3. Application Process

  • Water Tank Setup: Fill a tank with water and ensure it’s deep enough for the parts to be submerged.
  • Film Activation: Place the hydrographic film on the water surface and spray an activator over it. This activates the film and prepares it for dipping.
  • Dipping: Slowly submerge the car part into the water, allowing the film to wrap around it. Pull it out carefully to avoid bubbles and distortions.

4. Finishing Touches

  • Rinse and Dry: Rinse the dipped part to remove excess film and let it dry completely.
  • Clear Coat: Apply a clear coat to protect the design and enhance durability.

5. Curing

  • Allow the parts to cure fully according to the paint and clear coat manufacturer’s instructions.

Tips

  • Practice: If you're new to hydro dipping, practice on smaller items first.
  • Environment: Ensure you work in a well-ventilated area and use protective gear.
  • Patience: Allow adequate time for drying and curing to achieve the best results.

Liquid wrapping, also known as sprayable vinyl or peelable paint, is a technique used to apply a flexible, rubber-like coating to various surfaces, including vehicles, furniture, electronics, and more. Similar to plasti dip, liquid wrapping involves spraying a liquid polymer-based solution onto a surface, which dries to form a protective, peelable layer. Liquid wrap products typically come in spray cans or larger containers for use with spray guns, allowing for easy application and customization.

Key Features and Benefits of Liquid Wrapping:

  1. Customization: Liquid wrapping offers a wide range of color options, finishes, and effects, allowing for customization of surfaces to match individual preferences or branding requirements.
  2. Protective Coating: Once dried, liquid wrap forms a durable, flexible, and weather-resistant coating that protects surfaces from scratches, chips, UV rays, moisture, and corrosion.
  3. Temporary: Liquid wrap is temporary and peelable, meaning it can be easily removed from surfaces without causing damage. This makes it ideal for individuals who want to change the appearance of their belongings temporarily or try out different colors or designs.
  4. DIY-Friendly: Liquid wrapping can be applied by individuals with basic DIY skills using spray cans or larger containers and spray guns. With proper preparation and application techniques, professional-looking results can be achieved at home.
  5. Versatility: Liquid wrap can be used on a variety of surfaces, including metal, plastic, wood, glass, and more. It's commonly used to customize vehicles, such as cars, motorcycles, and bicycles, but can also be applied to furniture, electronics, and other items.
  6. Cost-Effective: Liquid wrap is generally more affordable than traditional paint or vinyl wrapping, making it a cost-effective option for customizing surfaces. It eliminates the need for expensive equipment or professional services, allowing enthusiasts to achieve their desired look without breaking the bank.
  7. Reversibility: One of the primary benefits of liquid wrap is its reversibility. If you decide you no longer want the coating on your surface or want to change the color or design, the liquid wrap can be peeled off easily without damaging the underlying surface.

Liquid wrapping, also known as spray-on wrap or peelable paint, is a technique used to coat surfaces with a flexible and protective layer of liquid polymer. This process is primarily used for vehicles, but it can also be applied to various other surfaces like furniture, electronics, and even walls.

Here's an overview of the liquid wrapping process:

  1. Surface Preparation: Before applying the liquid wrap, the surface must be thoroughly cleaned and dried to ensure proper adhesion. Any dirt, grease, or existing coatings should be removed.
  2. Masking: Areas that you don't want to be coated, such as windows, lights, and trim, need to be masked off using tape and paper. This ensures that only the intended surface receives the liquid wrap.
  3. Application: Liquid wrapping products are typically applied using a spray gun, similar to how paint is applied. The liquid is sprayed evenly onto the surface in several coats to achieve the desired thickness and coverage. It's essential to apply the liquid wrap evenly to prevent drips and inconsistencies.

Spray wrap has matt finish and isn't protected against fuel or staining from day to day use. To enhance your liquid wrap further you can add a glossifier finish which provides a OEM finish.

Features and Benefits of the Glossifier

  • Enhanced Appearance: It adds a glossy sheen to any item, making it more similar to a traditional paint job or a high-quality vinyl wrap.
  • Versatility: It can be applied over any colour, offering customization options to achieve the desired level of glossiness. Multiple coats can increase the gloss effect.

  • Easy Application: Like the base, Glossifier is easy to apply. It can be sprayed on, and no professional tools or skills are required for a basic application.
  • Removability: The Glossifier layer does not affect the removability of the underlying spray wrap. The coated item can still be returned to its original state by peeling off the wrap, provided it was applied thickly enough.

How to apply the Glossifier

  1. Preparation: Ensure that the base coat is completely dry and clean. Any dirt or oil on the surface can affect the finish of the Glossifier.
  2. Shaking: Shake the can of Glossifier well before use to mix the contents thoroughly, ensuring an even application.
  3. Testing: It's a good idea to test the Glossifier on a small, inconspicuous area first to ensure it reacts well with the base coat and to gauge the gloss level.
  4. Application: Spray the Glossifier in a well-ventilated area, applying thin, even coats. Hold the can 6-8 inches away from the surface and spray in a sweeping motion to avoid drips and runs.
  5. Layering: For a higher gloss finish, allow the first coat to dry for about 30 minutes before applying additional coats. Typically, 2-3 coats are sufficient, but you can add more depending on the desired level of shine.
  6. Drying: Allow the final coat to dry thoroughly. While it might be dry to the touch relatively quickly, a full cure can take up to 24 hours.

Maintenance and Care

  • Cleaning: Use gentle cleaning solutions and avoid abrasive materials that could scratch the Glossifier surface.
  • Protection: Although Glossifier adds durability, it's wise to protect the surface from harsh chemicals and extreme conditions that might compromise the finish.

Considerations

  • Environment: Application conditions can affect the outcome. Avoid applying in extremely cold or humid conditions to ensure the best finish.
  • Finish Variation: The final gloss level can vary based on the base color, number of coats, and application technique. Experimenting on a test piece can help predict the outcome on a larger project.

The finish is fuel and chemical resistant. Gloss is scratch resistant, but (not scratch proof). The wrap is then fully flat and mopped to give a show shine, better than OEM finish by far.

Liquid wrapping, also known as spray-on wrap or peelable paint, is a technique used to coat surfaces with a flexible and protective layer of liquid polymer. This process is primarily used for vehicles, but it can also be applied to various other surfaces like furniture, electronics, and even walls.

Here's an overview of the liquid wrapping process:

  1. Surface Preparation: Before applying the liquid wrap, the surface must be thoroughly cleaned and dried to ensure proper adhesion. Any dirt, grease, or existing coatings should be removed.
  2. Masking: Areas that you don't want to be coated, such as windows, lights, and trim, need to be masked off using tape and paper. This ensures that only the intended surface receives the liquid wrap.
  3. Application: Liquid wrapping products are typically applied using a spray gun, similar to how paint is applied. The liquid is sprayed evenly onto the surface in several coats to achieve the desired thickness and coverage. It's essential to apply the liquid wrap evenly to prevent drips and inconsistencies.
  4. Drying/Curing: After the liquid wrap is applied, it needs time to dry and cure. The drying time varies depending on factors such as temperature, humidity, and the specific product used. Some liquid wraps require heat curing to accelerate the drying process.
  5. Finishing: Once the liquid wrap is fully dried and cured, any masking tape and paper are removed. The surface may require additional finishing touches, such as trimming excess material around edges and seams.

Liquid wrapping offers several advantages over traditional paint:

  • Removability: One of the key benefits of liquid wrap is that it can be peeled off without damaging the underlying surface. This makes it ideal for temporary color changes or for protecting the original paint of a vehicle.
  • Customization: Liquid wraps are available in a wide range of colors, finishes, and effects, allowing for customization to suit individual preferences.
  • Protection: Liquid wraps provide a protective barrier against UV rays, chemicals, abrasions, and minor impacts, helping to preserve the surface underneath.
  • Cost-Effectiveness: Liquid wrapping can be more cost-effective than traditional painting methods, especially for temporary or experimental finishes.

Overall, liquid wrapping is a versatile and practical solution for enhancing and protecting surfaces, whether it's for automotive applications or other creative projects.

pages.html:
Printed graphics for your race car and support vehicles

Your Race Car Graphics need to represent your business and it's sponsors. Ensuring your business stands out on the track will not only catch the eye of spectators, but also potential sponsors.

Whether you are looking for some simple graphics for your race car or a full wrap, we have the knowledge and expertise to make your vehicle stand out from the rest. We can support your project from start to finishing including any support vehicles and trailers.

Creating race car graphics involves a blend of design principles, technical skills, and an understanding of the racing culture. Here are some steps and tips to create appealing race car graphics:

Steps to Create Race Car Graphics

Conceptualization:
Research: Look into different race car graphics for inspiration. Pay attention to colour schemes, patterns, and themes used by various racing teams.
Theme Selection: Decide on a theme that aligns with the car’s purpose, sponsor branding, or the driver’s personality.

Designing:
Software Selection: Use graphic design software like Adobe Illustrator, CorelDRAW, or specialised vehicle wrap design software.
Template Use: Obtain a high-quality template of the car model. This ensures the design fits perfectly on the car’s surface.
Sketching: Start with rough sketches to layout your ideas. Focus on key areas like the hood, sides, roof, and rear of the car.

Graphic Elements:
Colours: Choose vibrant colors that stand out. Make sure the colors match or complement the sponsor’s logos.
Logos and Branding: Place sponsor logos strategically to ensure visibility. Ensure logos are in vector format for scalability.
Patterns and Shapes: Incorporate stripes, flames, geometric shapes, or other dynamic patterns that convey speed and energy.
Text: Add necessary text like the car number, driver’s name, and sponsor taglines. Use bold and readable fonts.

Finalizing the Design:
Mockup: Create a mockup of the car with the graphics applied. This helps visualize the final outcome and make necessary adjustments.
Proofing: Double-check all elements for accuracy, alignment, and quality. Ensure all sponsor requirements are met.
Approval: Get approval from stakeholders (sponsors, racing team, driver) before proceeding to production.

Production and Application:
Print: Use high-quality vinyl wraps for printing the design. Ensure the printing service can handle large-format prints.
Installation: Hire professionals to apply the wrap to the car to avoid bubbles, wrinkles, and misalignment.

Tips for Effective Race Car Graphics

High Contrast: Ensure there is a high contrast between the car’s base color and the graphics to make the design stand out.
Flow with the Car’s Shape: Design elements should flow with the car’s contours to enhance the aerodynamic feel.
Visibility: Ensure that key information (e.g., car number, main sponsor) is visible from a distance.
Durability: Use materials and designs that can withstand harsh racing conditions (e.g., high speed, weather elements).
Innovation: Stay updated with the latest design trends and incorporate innovative elements to make the car unique.

Primary Colors: Red, Blue, Yellow, Black
Accent Colors: White, Silver, Neon Green
Pattern Examples:
Flames: Classic for speed and aggression.

pages.html:
A printed wall wrap is a large vinyl graphic or decal that is printed with digital images or designs and then applied directly to walls or surfaces. Wall wraps can transform the appearance of a room, building exterior, office, or retail space, providing a significant visual impact. They're used for decoration, branding, advertising, and wayfinding purposes, both indoors and outdoors.

Here are a few key points about printed wall wraps:

Types of Wall Wraps

Indoor Wall: Used to decorate interior spaces, enhance brand identity, or convey messages within offices, stores, restaurants, and homes.

Outdoor Wall: Designed to withstand weather elements, used for exterior branding, advertising, and beautifying buildings or spaces.

Temporary Wall: Ideal for events, promotions, or seasonal advertising, these are easier to remove and often made with less permanent adhesive.

Permanent Wall: Made with durable materials and adhesives intended for long-term use, perfect for branding or long-standing decoration.

Materials

Vinyl: The most common material, known for its durability and versatility. There are various types of vinyl, including options suitable for textured surfaces.

Fabric: Some wall wraps are printed on fabric for a different texture and aesthetic. Fabric wraps are often used indoors.

Specialty Materials: Reflective, metallic, or glow-in-the-dark vinyls are used for specific effects or functionalities.

Design and Printing

Custom Designs: Wall wraps can be customized with virtually any design, including photographic images, illustrations, text, and complex graphics.

Digital Printing: High-quality digital printers are used to produce vivid colors and detailed images on the wrap material.

Application

Surface Preparation: The surface must be clean, dry, and smooth for the best adhesion.

Professional Installation: Installing large wall wraps usually requires skilled professionals to ensure it's done correctly without bubbles or wrinkles.

  • Durability: With proper installation and care, wall wraps can last for years. Their lifespan depends on factors like material quality, environmental conditions, and whether they're placed indoors or outdoors.

Benefits

Visual Appeal: They dramatically change the look of a space or building.

Branding and Marketing: Effective for reinforcing brand identity and messaging.

Versatility: Can be applied to various surfaces, including drywall, brick, and concrete.

Cost-Effective: In comparison to traditional painting or wall treatments, wraps offer a durable and impactful alternative.

Using only the best materials from 3M and Metamark, you can rest assured your graphics will last for years.

Whether for commercial use to enhance brand presence or to personalize a residential space, printed wall wraps offer a creative and impactful solution to transform any space.

posts.title: Shop Signs in Norwich: A Winter Visibility Checklist
posts.excerpt: Will customers notice your shop sign on a dark afternoon? Use this checklist to assess visibility and prepare a clearer brief for a new sign.
posts.html:
When planning shop signs in Norwich, check how clearly someone can identify your business from the pavement after dark—not just how the design looks on a screen. Shorter winter days make contrast, viewing distance and lighting more important. Before ordering a new sign, visit the site at the times customers are likely to arrive and note what they can actually see.

Check your shop sign from the customer’s viewpoint

Start across the road, then approach along each pavement customers might use. Can you read the business name without stopping? Is the entrance obvious? A sign that looks prominent from directly outside may be hidden by a projecting building, street furniture or another shopfront from farther away.

Repeat the check in daylight and after dusk. Take photographs from roughly eye level, but use them as a reminder rather than a substitute for looking in person: a phone camera can make a dim scene appear brighter than it feels. Note any nearby lights that create glare or draw attention away from your sign.

If several messages compete for space, decide which one matters most. Usually, people need to recognise the business and find the entrance before they can absorb smaller details. A simple hierarchy—name first, supporting information second—will often work harder than filling every available area.

Make shop signs in Norwich readable after dark

Letter size depends on viewing distance and how quickly people pass. Stand where your intended audience will first see the sign and ask whether the main words are easy to distinguish. Fine type, tightly spaced lettering and long lines are harder to read at a glance, particularly in rain or low light.

Contrast matters as much as colour choice. Dark lettering on a light background, or light lettering on a dark background, can help the key message stand out. Check physical samples where possible: colours on a backlit screen may not represent how a finished material will look outside. A glossy finish can also produce distracting reflections under some lighting.

Illumination is worth considering if visibility during darker hours is important, but it is not the only answer. Existing street lighting, neighbouring signs, the building frontage and the direction people approach all affect the result. Ask a sign maker to explain suitable options for your site rather than choosing a lit sign from a photograph alone. If you are weighing up types of exterior building signs, include an evening photograph with your enquiry.

Inspect the existing sign before winter weather takes its toll

A visibility check is also a chance to look for maintenance issues. From a safe position, check whether panels appear secure and level, whether lettering is peeling or faded, and whether dirt is obscuring the design. Do not climb or attempt to inspect electrical components yourself; arrange an appropriate professional assessment if something appears loose or damaged.

Look at the whole frontage, not only the main fascia. Window displays can block sightlines to a sign, while an unclear door graphic may leave visitors unsure which entrance to use. If you are planning a refresh, take measurements and photographs of the fascia, windows and nearby obstructions. Record where the sign must be readable from and whether access for fitting might be restricted.

For a new or replacement sign, ask about materials and finishes suited to the proposed location, along with how the sign will be fitted. Exposure to wind and rain, mounting surface and access can all influence the specification. If permission may be needed for changes to the frontage or illumination, check the requirements for your premises before committing to a design.

Prepare a useful brief before requesting a quote

A clear brief helps a sign maker recommend an appropriate solution. Include your address, photographs taken by day and after dark, approximate dimensions, the wording you need and any existing brand artwork. Explain whether the priority is recognition from the road, helping pedestrians find the entrance, or both.

Also mention your preferred materials or finish if you have one, but leave room for alternatives. Ask what affects the quote, including sign size, material, illumination and fitting access. For shop and building signs, request clarity on the site survey, design proof and fitting before work proceeds. You can explore shop and building signs while gathering ideas, and use signage design as a supporting starting point if the artwork needs attention.

Frequently asked questions

Does every shop sign need illumination in winter?

No. Whether it helps depends on when people need to find you, the light already available and how the sign is positioned. Check visibility at the relevant time before deciding.

Should I replace a sign that looks dull after dark?

Not necessarily. First check whether dirt, poor contrast, glare or an obstruction is the main problem. That assessment will make any discussion about repair, redesign or replacement more useful.

What should I send with a shop sign enquiry?

Send frontage photographs from several approaches, approximate dimensions, required wording and any relevant access details. Evening photographs are especially helpful if after-dark visibility is your concern.
